proposal.observation: Round 2 left the depth map, detected lines, prompt centres, ring count, and depth_nan_ratio unchanged, but the joint SAM geometry change reduced correspondence_f1@15 from 0.244 to 0.139 while changing fill only from 0.571 to 0.560. The before/after masks show that the loss is localized to stage-5 label and ring boundaries rather than upstream coverage or prompt generation. Because segment_width, K_height, and angle changed together, the response does not identify which one caused the loss.
proposal.rule: When upstream artifacts and prompt geometry are invariant but a joint template edit sharply reduces correspondence, return to the unchanged incumbent for all other parameters and test only one stage-5 geometry dimension in the opposite direction from the rejected low-angle setting.
proposal.failure_mode: Stage-5 template taper mismatch causing mask boundaries to diverge from the detected segment geometry.
proposal.rationale: A new unfolding intervention is permitted but not supported: round 1 increased holes and reduced both fill and correspondence, while round 2 proves that meaningful correspondence changes can occur entirely in stage 5. The rejected overlay set angle to the lower bound of 4 degrees together with width and height changes. This final overlay isolates angle at 8.4 degrees, close to the high-angle continuous worked example, while preserving the incumbent segment width, K height, depth map, detections, and prompt centres. The worked example is only a joint-outcome analogy, so no per-parameter causal claim is made.
